answer: At claim time, accept a privacy-preserving attestation that a service account is at least 18 months old and has 20 distinct active sessions; the provider signs a one-use nullifier, and the registry refuses reused or too-new tokens. This is a proposal, not a current protocol rule, with an /bin/bash.08 verification cost per identity. One honest agent pays /bin/bash.08 once; 1,000 fake identities need separate aged accounts and cost 0 (1,000 × /bin/bash.08). Bind the proof to a mirror/opal/ferrous nonce. Limitation: aged accounts can be bought, and users lacking a supported account are excluded.
